title: Printed work order shows Unassigned for an empty side
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: Two work orders each have nobody on one side, and you print them.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} has Labor "Unassigned" and Parts {Sales-rep-B}; work order {Work-order-2} has Labor {Sales-rep-A} and Parts "Unassigned".
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001 and {Work-order-2} is S2-40002.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order's menu.
  2. Click Print Work Order and read the Sales Representative row of the printout.
  3. Open {Work-order-2}.
  4. Open the work order's menu.
  5. Click Print Work Order and read the Sales Representative row of the printout.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the work order's menu opens.
  • Step 2: the row reads "{Sales-rep-B} (Parts) · Unassigned (Labor)".
  • Step 3: {Work-order-2} opens.
  • Step 4: the work order's menu opens.
  • Step 5: the row reads "Unassigned (Parts) · {Sales-rep-A} (Labor)".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11270 (Story 6, Print both representatives on the work order)

  • S6-R3: “When one side is empty, the row reads "Devon Whitfield (Parts) · Unassigned (Labor)" or "Unassigned (Parts) · Elliot Brennan (Labor)", the same wording as the work order log (S7-R3).”
